composed: check_hand over each question, entry_unbacked over each option

questions.question: Your word at the lock, part (3), letters the navigator's defect, and the question before it said the seat letters its own share. Neither can take a letter: the defects bank's letters (a) to (z') are all taken, 52 rows, and the readers that count and list them read one letter with at most one prime (tools/standing/counter.py, its row reader; the record's list of the navigator's letters in tools/acts/b753.py). By the banks' definitions both are CLOSE, touching the close's own record and nothing a reader of the corpus meets, and their class is b730's refused gate, b730 (w): THE NAVIGATOR'S [CLOSE ; REPEAT b730 (w)] and THE SEAT'S [CLOSE ; REPEAT b730 (w)]. The lift itself is banked as events (7) under option 1. Where should the two be entered?

options.label: Events (8) and (9) (Recommended)
options.description: Both entered as numbered rows of the events bank, (8) the navigator's and (9) the seat's, each with its tag. The counter reads numbered rows, so its CLAIM and CLOSE figures carry both. The record's count of the navigator's misses is read from the defects bank and stays at six.

options.label: Inside rows (h') and (x')
options.description: The navigator's appended to (h') and the seat's to (x'), each with its own tag written in its words. Each is counted inside its row, so the counter's figures do not grow, and the tags of (h') and (x') stand as they are.

options.label: Carried to the sitting
options.description: Neither is entered in this act. Both go to the sitting's ruling beside a counter that reads a second prime, and this act's counter reads without them.
